name: Environment Setup
description: This block sets up the environment by importing necessary libraries and configuring API keys for OpenAI and Tavily. It ensures that the application has access to the required services for document processing and language model interactions.

name: Document Loading
description: This block loads PDF documents from a specified directory using the DirectoryLoader and PyMuPDFLoader. It prepares the documents for further processing by extracting their content into a structured format.

name: Text Processing
description: This block defines a function to calculate the token length of text and initializes a text splitter to divide the loaded documents into manageable chunks. It processes the loaded documents into smaller segments for easier handling in subsequent steps.

name: Chunk Length Calculation
description: This block calculates the number of document chunks created from the loaded loan knowledge resources. It provides a quick overview of how many segments are available for processing.

name: Embedding Model Initialization
description: This block initializes the OpenAI embeddings model, which will be used to convert the text chunks into vector representations for efficient retrieval. This is a crucial step for enabling semantic search capabilities.

name: Vector Store Creation
description: This block creates a vector store using the Qdrant library, which stores the document chunks along with their embeddings. This allows for efficient retrieval of relevant documents based on user queries.

name: Retriever Initialization
description: This block initializes a retriever from the vector store, which will be used to fetch relevant document chunks based on user queries. It sets up the mechanism for retrieving context during the response generation phase.

name: Prompt Template Definition
description: This block defines a chat prompt template that structures the context and query for the language model. It specifies how the model should respond based on the provided context and user query.

name: Chat Model Initialization
description: This block initializes the OpenAI chat model that will be used to generate responses based on the context retrieved from the vector store. It sets up the model for interaction with the user queries.

name: State Definition and RAG Graph Construction
description: This block defines the state structure for the RAG system and constructs the state graph that outlines the sequence of operations for retrieving documents and generating responses. It establishes the workflow for the RAG system.

name: RAG Graph Invocation
description: This block invokes the RAG graph with a sample question about student loans, demonstrating how the system can be used to retrieve information and generate a response.

name: Dynamic ArXiv Paper Fetching (Commented Out)
description: This block contains commented-out code for dynamically fetching papers from ArXiv based on a search query. It outlines how to create a RAG system with dynamically fetched content, but is not currently active in the execution flow.

name: Agent and Tool Initialization
description: This block imports necessary libraries and initializes various agents and tools for handling different tasks such as searching, retrieving information, and managing documents. It sets up the foundation for the collaborative workflow among agents.

name: Agent Node Definition
description: This block defines a function that creates an agent node for the state graph. It invokes the agent with the current state and returns the result as a message. This function is used to integrate agents into the workflow.

name: Agent Creation Functions
description: This block defines functions to create various agents for different roles in the system, such as a search agent, a research agent, and a team supervisor. Each agent is tailored to perform specific tasks within the collaborative workflow.

name: Team Supervisor Creation
description: This block defines a function to create a team supervisor agent that manages the workflow among different agents. It ensures that tasks are assigned appropriately and that the overall process is coordinated.

name: Tavily Search Tool Initialization
description: This block initializes the Tavily search tool, which will be used by the search agent to fetch up-to-date information. It sets the maximum number of results to be retrieved during searches.

name: Information Retrieval Tool Definition
description: This block defines a tool for retrieving information using the RAG system. It allows the user to query the system and receive responses based on the context retrieved from the vector store.

name: Document Management Functions
description: This block defines various functions for managing documents, including creating outlines, reading, writing, and editing documents. These functions facilitate the handling of text files within the system.

name: Document Writing State Definition
description: This block defines the state structure for the document writing process, including messages, team members, and the current files being worked on. It sets up the context for managing document-related tasks.

name: Document Writing Agent Creation
description: This block creates various agents for managing document writing tasks, including a document writer, note taker, copy editor, and empathy editor. Each agent is designed to handle specific aspects of the document creation process.

name: Document Writing Workflow Graph Construction
description: This block constructs the state graph for the document writing process, integrating all the agents and defining the workflow among them. It establishes the sequence of operations and how agents interact with each other.

name: Authoring Graph Visualization
description: This block visualizes the constructed authoring graph, displaying the workflow among the various agents involved in the document writing process. It provides a graphical representation of how tasks are managed and executed.

name: Authoring Chain Execution
description: This block defines the execution chain for the authoring process, allowing for the input of a user request and managing the flow of messages among the agents. It sets up the interaction model for generating responses based on user queries.
